This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Take Five: 3 + 2**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Bass lines](index.qmd#bass)

## The pattern

For 5/4: root on 1, fifth on the and of 2, then the root on 4 and 5.

It belongs in *Swing*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Ebm7|Bbm7|Ebm7|Bbm7" data-tempo="168" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-meter="5/4" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Take Five: 3 + 2","opts":{"bassFeel":"takefive"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Held roots (the bass voice)

Start with something simpler. The root of every chord, held until the next chord: the bass part of a four-part hymn.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass-held.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Ebm7|Bbm7|Ebm7|Bbm7" data-tempo="118" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-meter="5/4" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Held roots (the bass voice)","opts":{"bassFeel":"held"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Roots on 1 and 3

The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass-halves.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Ebm7|Bbm7|Ebm7|Bbm7" data-tempo="118" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-meter="5/4" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Take Five: 3 + 2, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Count 1-2-3, 4-5. Root on 1, fifth on the and of 2, root on 4 and 5. Say the count aloud until 5/4 stops feeling like 4/4 with a beat too many.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Ebm7|Bbm7|Ebm7|Bbm7" data-tempo="118" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-meter="5/4" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Take Five: 3 + 2","opts":{"bassFeel":"takefive"}},{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3 (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 168 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Ebm7|Bbm7|Ebm7|Bbm7" data-tempo="168" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-meter="5/4" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Take Five: 3 + 2","opts":{"bassFeel":"takefive"}}]'></div>
